body:
This normally happens when a file gets onto a filesystem with an encoding it shouldn't have. Syncthing can't deal with it automatically because it's unexpected.

If you don't need the file you should manually delete it.

Converting filenames from NFD to NFC with `convmv` solved this issue for me
(Mac OS X uses NFD while everything else uses NFC.).

Convert all files in a directory from NFD to NFC:
`convmv -r -f utf8 -t utf8 --nfc --notest .`

Convert all files in a directory from NFC to NFD:
`convmv -r -f utf8 -t utf8 --nfd --notest .`

On Fri, Jun 27, 2014 at 9:50 AM, jpjp notifications@github.com wrote:

> This normally happens when a file gets onto a filesystem with an encoding
> it shouldn't have. Syncthing can't deal with it automatically because it's
> unexpected.
> 
> If you don't need the file you should manually delete it.
> 
> ## 
> 
> Reply to this email directly or view it on GitHub
> https://github.com/calmh/syncthing/issues/396#issuecomment-47316839.
What about converting the file names to something safe when transferring them? Bittorrent sync will turn "#<3_foobar.log" into #_3_foobar.log" when transferring the file from *nix to Windows.

I put them on a Mac in the Repo and synced to a linux and a windows box.

You have Symbols like ", < and | on Windows too, so it should be possible to sync the Files with original name.
Those file names contain characters not representable on windows (quotes, pipes, etc), hence the error message. This is as expected.

I'm getting this too.  Linux allows colons but Windows doesn't:

```
11:39:43: File name "Screenshot from 2014-08-17 08:56:39.png" contains invalid characters; marked as invalid.

11:39:43: File name "Screenshot from 2014-08-17 08:57:20.png" contains invalid characters; marked as invalid.

11:39:43: File name "Screenshot from 2014-08-17 10:58:07.png" contains invalid characters; marked as invalid.

11:39:43: File name "Screenshot from 2014-08-17 11:11:15.png" contains invalid characters; marked as invalid.

11:39:48: All remaining files failed to sync. Stopping repo "default".
```

It really need to rename the files to fit the filesystem they're on, not just give up and prevent data from syncing.  The original name should be remembered for syncing with filesystems that support it, but on filesystems that don't, they should be renamed.  We shouldn't have to rename dozens of files by hand.
also I'm still seeing these errors even _after_ renaming the files?

Yeah, there are two bugs here.
1. The repo shouldn't stop due to invalid file names; these are not i/o errors.
2. We shouldn't consider it a problem that we need to delete a file with an invalid file name when the file doesn't exist to start with.
I'm still getting this error, is there a new ticket tracking this bug or should this one be re-opened?
I think we forgot to reopen this.
What's the bug? My points from above are handled I think, and the presence of invalid file names is something we just have to log and live with.
Are they? From your message above it sounds that they aren't?
That's two years ago... But ah you may be right that we complain about deleted files maybe?

I feel like files should still be copied, albeit with invalid characters encoded in a manner that the target filesystem supports. Since Windows and NTFS is likely the target to complain the most, maybe the filenames could have their invalid characters URL encoded; like `%2A` for `*`, `%3A` for `:` and others? The target syncthing instance wouldn't need to keep a table mapping, it would just decode the parts back to the correct character.
That's #1734 and unrelated to what's going on here.
I've deleted comments that relate to the issue I linked above. I linked it for a reason.
This is now a proper sync error instead.
